notes.summary: Source and premise audit: the inspected arbitrary-field results supply continuous theory, while compactness, envelopes and equation results retain additional hypotheses. No general-valued higher-dimensional equation is granted.
notes.detailedSummary: Version-pinned primary proof units support the continuous operator, energy, regularization and local approachable-product inputs. The inspected classical compactness theorem is discrete-valued; the trivial-field compactness theorem and newer polyhedral theorem concern different domains. Arbitrary-field envelope differentiation in BGM assumes envelope continuity. The supplied completed-closure descent theorem is used only after independently establishing its operator and target antecedents. The unreviewed217 manuscript and unreviewed218 plan are research data, not premises.
notes.text:
The retained domain throughout the new draft is: K a complete real-valued non-Archimedean field of residue characteristic zero, including trivial and nondiscrete valuations and nonalgebraically-closed fields; X/K smooth, geometrically integral and projective of arbitrary dimension; L an actual ample rational line bundle. Smoothness, projectivity, algebraizability, ampleness and residue characteristic zero are retained. No torus invariance, skeleton or support restriction is imposed.

The applied continuous primary source is Boucksom–Eriksson, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3. Complete pertinent units inspected are Definitions 5.15 and 7.2; Proposition 5.16, Lemma 5.17 and the separation proof of Theorem 5.18; Lemma 7.4 and Corollaries 7.5–7.6; Example 7.12 and Theorem 7.14; Section 8.1, including Proposition 8.3, Lemma 8.6, Theorem 8.4 and its extension proof, Proposition 8.5 and signed dpsh calculus; Definition 9.13 and Proposition 9.14 with proof. Our actual ample bundles satisfy their semiample hypotheses, and smooth geometrically integral X satisfies geometric reducedness. Real PL weights include the trivial valuation. These inputs supply continuous measures and energy, not singular products or an equation theorem.

For continuous local products, Chambert-Loir–Ducros, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1, was inspected at its arbitrary-complete-field convention, complete Lemma 5.6.1, Proposition 5.6.2, Definition 5.6.3, Corollaries 5.6.5–5.6.6 and their local construction/gluing proofs, Proposition 5.4.6 with measure representation and uniqueness, and Section 6.4.1. The local weights used here are uniformly smoothly semipositive regularizable by BE, hence locally psh-approachable. No identification of arbitrary continuous CLD-psh functions with approachable functions is assumed. Smooth Stokes and positivity remain ordinary analytic foundations; their entire recursive development is not freshly reverified.

The scope audit read BGM, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.03847v1, Section 1.5, Theorem 3.1 with Lemma 3.2 and its complete derivative proof, and Theorem 3.4 with the complete Lemma 3.5 proof. Its arbitrary-field relative-volume derivative concerns continuous psh metrics. Envelope-energy differentiation and orthogonality assume continuity of envelopes; they are not a both-sign outer derivative at every singular E1 endpoint.

The complete BFJ Theorem 7.10 proof in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.0187v2 retains a complete discrete valuation field and residue characteristic zero. Its SNC-model topology and equicontinuity are not transplanted to a non-Noetherian valuation ring. The complete BJ Theorem 5.11 proof in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4 relates normalized compactness to the envelope property in its trivially valued setting. Wu, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1, was inspected at Theorem A and the complete Theorem 7.1 proof; its domain remains discrete or trivial, equicharacteristic zero. Botero–Mazzon–Pille–Schneider, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1, Theorem 3.36 has a compactness proof for a polyhedral psh cone; its Section 7 analytic applications concern selected Calabi–Yau tropicalizations over C((t)). This is not compactness of the full original potential cone. Pille–Schneider https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.04879v2 and the introduction of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.01697v1 were inspected for their continuous/singular and measure/potential boundaries. These checks do not prove exhaustive absence of another theorem.

The supplied completed-closure descent mathematical body grants the orbit quotient, all-point invariant singular-psh descent, extended-energy equality, unique invariant Radon lift and continuous-test-dual equality in its complete characteristic-zero smooth geometrically integral projective actual-ample domain. Its equation transfer requires explicit upstairs existence and every-solution uniqueness. Neither is granted. The supplied trivial-field equation and curve operator are compatible endpoints, not prerequisites of the new operator/locality proofs. Historical headings are not script certification.

The precise quote-free ledger is source-application-ledger.json with source-application-ledger.md. Caller bodies are preserved in inputs/G1.tex, inputs/G2.tex and inputs/G3.tex; unreviewed data in inputs/unreviewed217.tex and inputs/unreviewed218.json. Sources are preserved as rendered response snapshots under sources/. Hashes bind these response bytes, not downloaded PDF bytes. Direct downloading failed at the configured proxy; no configuration was changed. Rerun: python3 make_ledger.py. Caller bodies initially have no registered kernel note IDs; only the local IDs emitted in this submission appear in support.

notes.summary: Reconstructed draft proof of an arbitrary-field finite-energy mixed operator, raw mass, all-E1-test integrability, joint arbitrary decreasing weighted nets, energy and affine calculus. This operator theorem does not establish the prescribed-target equation.
notes.detailedSummary: On actual all-point fixed-bundle FS-net endpoints, an ordered PL energy-gap estimate constructs approximation-independent positive pure limits and positive mixed polarization of mass V=(L^n). Averaging yields integrability, and a two-potential energy estimate controls singular-test errors uniformly along decreasing nets. These give genuine weighted energy identities, polynomial affine differentiation, reference covariance and complete-field pushforward. No envelope continuity or normalized potential compactness is assumed.
notes.text:
Retain exactly the domain in n1. Put T=X^an and V=(L^n)>0, and choose a continuous psh reference metric ψ. An actual scalar u denotes ψ+u on every analytic point. PSH means an all-point decreasing-net endpoint of basepoint-free FS metrics on the fixed rational bundle, excluding the identically −∞ metric but retaining supported poles. Let C be its continuous subspace. For continuous u, write θ_u=dd^c(ψ+u) and define E(u)=(1/(n+1)) Σ_{j=0}^n ∫u θ_u^j θ_0^{n−j}. For singular u define E(u)=inf{E(v):v∈C,v≥u}, and E1={u:E(u)>−∞}. This definition precedes the singular operator. Constants satisfy E(u+c)=E(u)+Vc.

The draft proves a canonical positive symmetric mixed Radon operator MA on (E1)^n of raw mass V, extending the genuine continuous operator. It is independent of all continuous decreasing approximations. Every E1 test is integrable against every mixed output. Whenever all slots u_{r,i} decrease to E1 endpoints u_r and w_i decreases to w∈E1 on an arbitrary common directed index, the measures converge weakly and ∫w_i MA(u_{1,i},…,u_{n,i}) converges to ∫w MA(u_1,…,u_n). No arbitrary-measurable-net MCT is used.

Continuous calculus. Rational convex combinations of FS systems are FS by clearing denominators and tensoring section systems. Uniform closure gives real convexity of C. The continuous energy cocycle is
E(v)−E(u)=(1/(n+1)) Σ_{j=0}^n ∫(v−u) θ_v^j θ_u^{n−j}.
For a product Q of n−1 continuous semipositive curvatures, define D_Q(f,g)=−∫f dd^c g Q on continuous scalar differences of psh metrics, allowing auxiliary bundles. Uniform smooth semipositive regularization, compact boundaryless Stokes and positivity make D_Q symmetric and positive semidefinite. Passage to continuous data is justified by uniform convergence of scalar factors, weak convergence of signed products and their fixed total-variation bounds. Cauchy–Schwarz follows from positivity of D_Q(f+sg,f+sg). Continuous energy is concave, since its second derivative on a segment with difference d is −n D_{θ_t^{n−1}}(d,d).

Ordered estimate. For every real PL test f=h−k, with h,k FS metrics on an auxiliary ample A, take C_f=2||f||∞(A·L^{n−1}). For continuous u≤v, δ=v−u and Q_j=θ_u^j θ_v^{n−1−j}, each D_{Q_j}(f,f)≤C_f because the two positive auxiliary products have mass A·L^{n−1}. Factoring curvature differences gives
Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}D_{Q_j}(δ,δ)=∫δ(θ_u^n−θ_v^n)≤∫δ θ_u^n≤(n+1)(E(v)−E(u)).
Cauchy–Schwarz for each form and then the finite sum proves
|∫f(θ_v^n−θ_u^n)|≤√[n(n+1)C_f(E(v)−E(u))].
Real PL tests are uniformly dense on the full carrier, including supported points.

Energy limits. If actual usc psh u_i↓u with actual endpoint, then E(u_i)↓E(u), including −∞. Indeed, for any continuous psh majorant a≥u and ε>0, the compact closed sets {u_i−a≥ε} decrease to an empty intersection. Directedness and compactness give u_i≤a+ε on a tail, so inf_i E(u_i)≤E(a)+Vε. Infimize over a and let ε→0. Monotonicity gives the reverse inequality. With an identically −∞ endpoint, constant majorants −M force energies to −∞. Product-directed continuous approximation, continuous concavity and this exclusion argument show that finite positive convex combinations of E1 endpoints remain actual E1, with concave energy. Maxima remain E1 by continuous maxima, decreasing closure and energy monotonicity.

Radon net facts. For a finite Radon measure λ on a compact Hausdorff space, increasing directed nonnegative lsc g_i satisfy ∫sup_i g_i dλ=sup_i∫g_i dλ. At every strict level the supremum superlevel is a directed union of open sets. Inner compact subsets have finite subcovers dominated by one index. Inner regularity gives equality of superlevel masses; finite layer sums and truncation give the integral equality. For weak λ_a→λ and nonnegative lsc g, ∫g dλ≤liminf_a∫g dλ_a follows by approximating g from below with continuous functions using normality and inner regularity. Neither result permits arbitrary measurable-net MCT.

Pure construction. For any continuous psh u_a↓u∈E1, finite energy convergence and the ordered estimate make the genuine continuous measures Cauchy on each PL test; incomparable indices are compared to a common later stage. Uniform mass V and density extend the limit to a positive functional on C(T), with value V on 1. Riesz yields MA(u). For a second net v_b↓u, compare both with max(u_a,v_b) on the product index. All three energies tend to E(u), so the ordered error vanishes. This proves independence. A constant net gives genuine continuous agreement. For singular ordered u≤v, max of their continuous approximants decreases to v; passage to limits proves the same ordered estimate. It then gives weak convergence along arbitrary singular decreasing E1 nets.

Mixed construction. For nonempty I⊂{1,…,n}, set u_I=|I|^(−1)Σ_{r∈I}u_r. Define
MA(u_1,…,u_n)=(1/n!)Σ_{I≠∅}(−1)^{n−|I|}|I|^n MA(u_I).
At continuous stages, inclusion–exclusion kills every curvature monomial missing a label; the surviving product has coefficient n!. Thus the formula is the genuine continuous mixed measure. Simultaneous continuous approximation makes its limit positive of mass V; positivity is proved from these stages, not assumed for a signed expression. Approximation independence, symmetry and convex-affine dependence of each curvature slot follow by passage from continuous identities. Subset averages also prove mixed weak convergence for singular decreasing slots.

Integrability. A common constant reference shift makes a fixed finite family and chosen approximation tails nonpositive. Write B=−E≥0. For continuous w,u_1,…,u_n put z=(w+u_1+…+u_n)/(n+1). Concavity gives B(z)≤(B(w)+Σ B(u_r))/(n+1). All terms in B(z) are nonnegative. Its top term contains ∫(−w)θ_{u_1}…θ_{u_n} with coefficient n!/(n+1)^(n+2). Consequently
∫(−w)MA(u_1,…,u_n)≤[(n+1)^(n+1)/n!](B(w)+Σ B(u_r)).
First pass continuous curvature approximants with a fixed continuous test by weak convergence and energy convergence. Then decrease continuous test majorants to w; the Radon lsc-directed law on the fixed output proves the bound for actual inputs. Adding constants back gives absolute integrability of every E1 test. Each output gives zero mass to that test’s pole set; no uncountable common full-measure set is claimed.

Uniform singular-test error. For continuous w_k↓w∈E1 and u∈E1,
∫(w_k−w)MA(u)≤A_n[E((u+w_k)/2)−E((u+w)/2)], A_n=2^(n+1)(n+1).
For continuous u and j≥k, apply the ordered energy cocycle to h_k=(u+w_k)/2≥h_j=(u+w_j)/2. Keep the top term and use MA(h_k)≥2^(−n)MA(u); their difference is (w_k−w_j)/2. This proves the estimate with w_j. Directed lsc integration and energy continuity pass j to w. For singular u, decrease continuous approximants and use lsc portmanteau for w_k−w and finite convergence of both right-side energies.

Weighted convergence. If u_i↓u and w_k↓w continuously, the product-directed potentials (u_i+w_k)/2 decrease to (u+w)/2∈E1. Given ε>0, choose i_0,k_0 so their energy gaps to the endpoint are below ε. Since E((u_i+w)/2)≥E((u+w)/2), the preceding estimate bounds replacement of w by the fixed continuous w_{k_0} uniformly on the moving tail by A_nε, and similarly for the endpoint measure. Weak convergence at that fixed continuous test proves convergence for w. For singular moving weights w_i↓w, compactness gives w_i≤w_k+η on a tail. Hence
0≤∫(w_i−w)MA(u_i)≤∫(w_k−w)MA(u_i)+ηV.
The same uniform error, followed by ε,η→0, proves the moving-weight law. Finite polarization proves the full mixed weighted law.

Energy and differentiation. Apply the weighted law to every continuous energy term to obtain E(u)=(1/(n+1))Σ_j∫u MA(u^[j],0^[n−j]). The identical passage in the cocycle gives E(v)−E(u)=(1/(n+1))Σ_j∫(v−u)MA(v^[j],u^[n−j]). Differences are evaluated on the common finite-value full-measure sets. On u_t=(1−t)u+tv, continuous approximations give energy polynomials of degree at most n+1. Each derivative coefficient is a finite mixed integral with weight u or v, and the weighted law passes all coefficients to finite limits. The constant coefficient tends to E(u). Integration of this finite coefficient limit and energy continuity identify the limiting polynomial with E(u_t). Its derivative is ∫(v−u)MA(u_t), including one-sided endpoints. This is not unrestricted exchange of limits and derivatives, and is not an outer envelope derivative.

Covariance. A continuous psh reference change ψ′=ψ+b has the same absolute continuous majorants. The continuous cocycle and infimization give E_{ψ′}(u−b)=E_ψ(u)−E_ψ(b). Absolute approximation measures are unchanged, hence the class and operator are reference independent. For any complete real-valued extension F/K, pullback of defining FS nets retains their literal endpoints. Continuous energy equality and decreasing energy continuity prove E_F(u_F)=E_K(u). The genuine continuous mixed pushforward law passes to the weak limits by testing with f composed with the analytic projection, giving p_*MA_F(u_{1,F},…,u_{n,F})=MA_K(u_1,…,u_n). Geometric mass remains V, without a field-degree factor.

The complete draft proof is in P16.4-argument.md and standalone P16.4-paper.tex. Rerun: python3 build.py. This is an independently reconstructed, unverified mathematical proof from the continuous inputs in n1; the unreviewed217 theorem is not assumed. No prescribed-target existence or uniqueness follows merely from this operator.

notes.summary: New draft proof of strict Borel mixed max-locality and mixed/pure comparison over the retained arbitrary fields. It uses the reconstructed weighted operator, preserves poles and directed nets, and assumes no envelope theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: Continuous open locality is obtained from the exact CLD approachable-product sheaf and identified with BE measures. Uniform L1 approximation transports bounded Lipschitz functions of actual E1 tests through moving outputs. Diagonal weighted errors then pass strict-winner cutoffs to singular Borel sets. Raw mass gives mixed comparison; a finite chain of slot replacements gives pure comparison. These conclusions do not prove attainment or every-solution uniqueness.
notes.text:
Use n2’s retained domain, raw mass V and constructed operator. Let u,v∈E1, R=(r_2,…,r_n)∈(E1)^(n−1), and m=max(u,v); R is empty for n=1.

Continuous bridge. For continuous slots, MA(m,R) restricted to the open set {u>v} equals MA(u,R), and symmetrically for v. On a local trivialization of a cleared power of L, all local weights are uniformly smoothly semipositive regularizable, hence locally psh-approachable. The CLD product is a local sheaf construction. On the strict winner open set the maximum weight literally equals the winning weight, so their local products coincide. Positive top-current uniqueness identifies the local Radon measures. These products equal restrictions of the global BE operator by restricting the same smooth regularizations to compactly supported local smooth tests and using uniqueness of both limits. Logarithms of invertible transition functions have zero dd^c, so the local identifications glue. This uses the precise approachable hypothesis, not a general local psh equivalence.

Bounded Lipschitz transport. Suppose ρ_i are mixed outputs whose E1 slots decrease to E1 endpoints, with weak limit ρ. For fixed finite E1 tests b_1,…,b_q, bounded Lipschitz F:R^q→R and continuous f, the integrals ∫f F(b_1,…,b_q)dρ_i converge to the corresponding integral against ρ. To prove this, choose continuous b_{r,k}↓b_r. For a fixed tuple of approximation indices, n2’s fixed-weight law gives convergence of ∫(b_{r,k}−b_r)dρ_i to its endpoint value. These nonnegative endpoint errors decrease to zero by directed Radon integration. Choose one tuple making their finite sum small, then a moving tail on which it remains small. The Lipschitz bound controls the replacement error by ||f||∞Lip(F) times this sum. The fixed-stage composition is continuous, so weak convergence applies. Remove the tuple. Assigned values at poles are irrelevant because each involved measure integrates every test.

Singular locality. Take product-directed continuous approximants u_i↓u, v_i↓v and R_i↓R. Set m_i=max(u_i,v_i), ρ_i=MA(m_i,R_i), and σ_i=MA(u_i,R_i). Their endpoints are E1. Subtracting the moving- and fixed-weight limits gives ∫(u_i−u)dρ_i→0 and ∫(v_i−v)dρ_i→0, and both statements for σ_i. All differences are nonnegative on the per-measure finite-value sets.

For ε>0 define χ_ε(d)=0 if d≤0, d/ε if 0<d<ε, and 1 if d≥ε. Continuous locality gives ∫fχ_ε(u_i−v_i)dρ_i=∫fχ_ε(u_i−v_i)dσ_i. The diagonal L1 errors and the Lipschitz bound replace each stage cutoff by χ_ε(u−v) with vanishing error. The preceding fixed Borel transport passes both sides to the endpoint. Thus χ_ε(u−v)MA(m,R)=χ_ε(u−v)MA(u,R). Bounded Borel densities of finite Radon measures remain Radon, so continuous tests determine this equality. Sequential ε↓0 and ordinary dominated convergence on each fixed measure give
1_{u>v}MA(m,R)=1_{u>v}MA(u,R).
Interchanging u,v gives the other strict locality identity. Winner sets are Borel. Pole sets are null for each relevant output; literal common poles are ties and are never subtracted. No arbitrary measurable-net MCT or uncountable common null-set assertion enters.

Comparison. Put m_ε=max(u,v−ε). Constant shifts preserve curvature, and all measures have mass V. Strict locality gives
MA(v,R){u<v−ε}=MA(m_ε,R){u<v−ε}
≤V−MA(m_ε,R){u>v−ε}
=MA(u,R){u≤v−ε}≤MA(u,R){u<v}.
Sequential ε↓0 exhausts {u<v}, up to the pole-null sets. Hence MA(v,R){u<v}≤MA(u,R){u<v}. To obtain pure comparison, choose R successively with j copies of v and n−1−j copies of u, for j=0,…,n−1, and chain these one-slot inequalities. This yields MA(v){u<v}≤MA(u){u<v}. A single application does not suffice in higher dimension.

The proofs are preserved in P16.4-argument.md and P16.4-paper.tex; python3 build.py rebuilds them. The unreviewed218 plan is not a premise, and no feedback from its independent campaign was obtained. These draft results supply locality/comparison, not an equation theorem.

notes.summary: Draft variational consequences: finite continuous-test dual implies all-E1 integrability; pure outputs have finite dual; every solution maximizes the energy objective. Completed-closure operator and target antecedents are checked, but existence and all-point uniqueness remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: For prescribed positive Radon targets of raw mass V, the continuous-test dual extends exactly to all actual E1 tests when finite. Concavity and the affine derivative give a whole supporting plane and the exact dual cost of each pure output. Two solutions have zero mixed Dirichlet quantities, but this is not proved to imply equality modulo constants. The supplied descent body yields dual equality upstairs; the new implication then proves integrability of noninvariant upstairs tests. Actual upstairs existence and every-solution uniqueness are still missing.
notes.text:
For a prescribed positive Radon measure μ on T impose μ(T)=V and define J_ψ(μ)=sup_{v∈C}(E_ψ(v)−∫v dμ). Constants cancel because the mass is V. The intrinsic all-test condition is E1⊂L1(μ). The draft proves finite J implies that condition, but does not prove its converse for arbitrary targets in the general-valued higher-dimensional domain.

Indeed, take continuous u_a↓u∈E1 and a tail bounded above by C. The dual inequality gives ∫u_a dμ≥E(u_a)−J≥E(u)−J. Thus the increasing continuous nonnegative functions C−u_a have bounded integrals. Directed Radon integration proves integrability of u and convergence of these integrals. Energy continuity passes the objective to u. Since continuous competitors are E1, J equals the supremum of E(u)−∫u dμ over all actual E1 potentials.

For ν=MA(u), extended concavity and the genuine affine right derivative give the whole supporting plane
E(v)≤E(u)+∫(v−u)dMA(u), v∈E1.
All integrals are finite by n2. Thus every continuous-test objective at ν is at most E(u)−∫u dν. Continuous majorants of u have objectives tending to this value by energy continuity and directed integration on ν. Therefore J_ψ(MA(u))=E(u)−∫u dMA(u)<∞. In particular, every actual solution of MA(u)=μ globally maximizes E(v)−∫v dμ. This statement concerns every solution, not only a variationally constructed one.

If MA(u)=MA(v)=μ, both maximize that objective. Concavity makes their entire affine segment maximize; its energy is affine because its μ-integral is affine. For d=v−u, the energy polynomial has zero second derivative, hence −∫d dd^c d θ_{u_t}^{n−1}=0. Here the expression is defined by finite signed differences of the constructed mixed measures, with legitimate E1 test integrals. Its Bernstein coefficients D_j=−∫d dd^c d θ_u^j θ_v^{n−1−j} are nonnegative: continuous positivity passes through the weighted law. Positive interior Bernstein factors force every D_j=0. The draft does not identify this degeneracy with all-point equality of actual potentials modulo constants. It is a necessary every-solution consequence, not uniqueness.

A continuous reference change gives J_{ψ+b}(μ)=J_ψ(μ)−E_ψ(b)+∫b dμ; the correction is finite. Thus finite dual cost and all-test integrability are reference independent.

Completed closure. Apply the supplied accepted descent body only now, with C=completed algebraic closure of K, Y=X_C^an and the pulled-back reference. Residue characteristic zero persists. Its quotient, invariant actual-psh descent, energy equality, unique invariant Radon lift μ̃ and J_C(μ̃)=J_K(μ) hold in their exact retained domain. The operator antecedent is independently established upstairs by n2. Continuous naturality under valued-field isometries, transport of defining FS nets and approximation independence prove singular equivariance. The field pushforward law identifies the descended operator with the direct downstairs one; an invariant output is the unique invariant lift of its pushforward. Weighted pullback identities are already proved. Locality/comparison are supplied by n3.

If J_K(μ)<∞, dual equality gives J_C(μ̃)<∞. Applying the newly proved target implication upstairs shows that μ̃ integrates every upstairs E1 test, including noninvariant tests. This does not average unbounded singular potentials.

Equation transfer remains conditional. If actual upstairs existence for μ̃ and uniqueness modulo constants for every upstairs solution were proved, normalize a solution by sup_Y u=0. Equivariance and invariance of the target make all conjugates normalized solutions; uniqueness makes the potential invariant, so the supplied descent body descends it. Two downstairs solutions would lift to invariant outputs with the same pushforward, hence the same unique invariant lift, and upstairs uniqueness would descend. Neither equation antecedent is supplied here. Completed algebraic closure does not make a nondiscrete value group discrete. The supplied trivial-field equation gives no nontrivially valued equation, and the supplied curve operator gives no target existence conclusion.

These arguments and limitations are preserved in P16.4-argument.md and P16.4-paper.tex.

notes.summary: The standalone partial paper and reproducible evidence are complete, with candidate=false. Original P16.4 remains unresolved at actual-potential compactness, envelopes and outer differentiation, intrinsic target characterization/coercivity, attainment and every-solution uniqueness.
notes.detailedSummary: The draft reconstructs the arbitrary-field mixed operator and proves strict locality/comparison, but does not establish the unchanged prescribed-target existence-and-uniqueness theorem. Exact rational checks pass and existing tools compile a 12-page PDF in two LaTeX passes. Supporting notes use only emitted local IDs. Compilation, checks, hashes and source ledgers are observations rather than mathematical certification.
notes.text:
Original P16.4 is not solved. The operator, weighted calculus and comparison gaps of this draft are addressed in n2–n3, but these six equation inputs remain:

1. Compactness of a normalized space of actual fixed-bundle psh potentials, with all-point determination/closure ensuring that maximizing subnets have actual original potential endpoints. The needed energy upper semicontinuity and target-integral semicontinuity must hold in that topology. Compactness of T or of its mass-V measures is insufficient.
2. An actual all-point envelope/regularization theorem over nondiscrete fields, or a precise substitute providing P(u+tf)∈E1 for actual u∈E1 and continuous f with both signs of t. Orthogonality/contact must concern the genuine operator. Noetherian resolution over k[t] or a reduced-fiber theorem does not establish this over an arbitrary valuation ring.
3. Both-sign outer differentiation d/dt|_0 E(P(u+tf))=∫f dMA(u). The proved affine derivative supplies only psh-segment directions; continuous relative-volume differentiation does not replace the missing singular envelope argument.
4. The converse from integrability of every actual E1 test to finite dual cost for arbitrary prescribed targets, plus quantitative coercivity sufficient for actual attainment. Only finite-dual-to-integrability is proved. The special quadratic contraction after generic trivial normalization cannot be transplanted unchanged to a general reference measure.
5. Actual attainment of the dual objective for every prescribed target satisfying the correct condition, followed by its Euler equation. If a maximizer and item 3 were available, the envelope sandwich u−|t|||f||∞≤P(u+tf)≤u+tf and maximality would give E(P(u+tf))−E(u)−t∫f dμ≤0. Both derivative signs would force MA(u)=μ against every continuous test. Neither antecedent is established; μ is never chosen by naming an energy derivative.
6. Uniqueness modulo one constant for every actual solution. Comparison and the mixed degeneracy in n4 are proved, but a domination/determination argument upgrading them to literal all-point equality is missing.

These are gaps of this submission, not impossibility theorems or an exhaustive negative claim about the literature. The intended target has positive Radon raw mass V=(L^n), with finite J_ψ and the desired intrinsic all-E1 characterization. Positive residue characteristic and nonample classes are separate axes and are not silently included. The zero-dimensional geometrically integral case is immediate and does not close the residual higher-dimensional scope.

Deliverables are P16.4-paper.tex, P16.4-paper.pdf and P16.4-argument.md in the supplied workspace, together with source-application-ledger.json/.md, retained inputs and source snapshots, structured-notes.json and submission.json. The paper is a standalone unverified draft containing the full arguments and precise residual inputs.

On the specified interval tree [0,2] with unit edges and reference atoms 1 at 0,1,2, raw mass is 3. All 125 nodal triples in {−2,−1,0,1,2}^3 were enumerated; 35 have positive curvature. All 1225 ordered pairs were checked, inserting 160 total strict interior crossings. Max curvature remained positive of mass 3; strict locality, comparison and the epsilon complement argument held at ε=1/2,1,3/2. The cutoff Lipschitz inequality was exhausted on 675 specified rational cases. These are exhaustive finite algebra/model observations, not certification on analytic varieties.
